root_idea.summary: The root centers on something passing away, lacking lasting reality, or ceasing to have effect; this yields the senses of nullity, falsehood, invalidation, and futility.
root_idea.development: From the basic idea of disappearance or brief continuance, the root develops into describing what is false, void, ineffective, or unprofitable, and into causative uses meaning to annul or render something futile. The related sense of a hero is explained as one who exposes himself to destruction or makes danger and injury of no account.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic form is plural, but the supported dictionary citation form is the singular active participle مُبْطِلٌ.

senses.definition: To become void, futile, or without effect; to go for nothing.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of an act, deed, assertion, or other thing that loses its efficacy or value and becomes of no account.

senses.definition: To nullify, annul, or render void and ineffectual; to make something go for nothing.
senses.usage_conditions: A transitive causative use applying whether the object is true or false, valid or invalid. Quranic constructions include rendering deeds vain, proving a claim or practice false, and annulling falsehood.

senses.definition: Falsehood; that which is untrue, unfounded, unreal, invalid, futile, worthless, or without effective purpose.
senses.usage_conditions: May describe or denote sayings, beliefs, claims, deeds, affairs, or things lacking truth, soundness, efficacy, or lasting value. In constructions with بِ, it can express acting by or with falsehood, wrongfully, or without legitimate basis.

senses.definition: In a reported Quranic interpretation, belief in a plurality of gods or polytheistic belief.
senses.usage_conditions: This is a specialized interpretive application of الباطل and should not replace its general sense of falsehood or invalidity.

senses.definition: In certain Quranic interpretations, al-bāṭil denotes Iblīs; its plural may denote devils or enchanters.
senses.usage_conditions: A specialized referential interpretation of الباطل in particular Quranic expressions, distinct from the ordinary abstract sense of falsehood.

senses.definition: One who utters or performs false or vain things; a falsifier.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of a person whose speech or conduct has no truth or reality, including one who embellishes speech with lies or makes false claims.

senses.definition: One who invalidates or seeks to annul what is true.
senses.usage_conditions: A Quranic use emphasizing the agent who attempts to nullify or discredit the truth, rather than merely uttering a false statement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a person's blood: to go unavenged and uncompensated; of a slain person, to be killed without retaliation or blood-wit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in the idiomatic expressions بَطَلَ دَمُهُ and ذَهَبَ دَمُهُ بُطْلًا.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be idle, unoccupied, or without work.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A personal use, especially of someone who has no employment or current occupation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Idleness, or being diverted from what would bring profit in this world or the next.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun denotes unproductive inactivity or diversion from beneficial activity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In speech, to jest, joke, or speak without seriousness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a discourse-related use describing a lack of earnestness, not merely the falsity of the content.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become courageous, brave, or strong-hearted in war or fighting; sometimes, to affect or force oneself to be courageous.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The bravery sense is distinct from the Form I sense of becoming futile and is associated with the noun بَطَلٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The pursuit of vain or frivolous diversion or sport, together with foolish or ignorant conduct.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An abstract noun describing unprofitable amusement and conduct.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To speak falsely, lie, or make a false claim or demand for oneself; to claim what is not right or just.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This lexical branch concerns the speaker or claimant and is distinct from the causative use meaning to annul an object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take turns among themselves in saying or doing false, vain, wrong, or futile things.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal or alternating construction describing people sharing out false or futile speech or conduct.
An attested, though qualified, use of the Form V verb distinct from its reciprocal use concerning false or futile speech and conduct.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A courageous, brave, or strong-hearted person, especially in war; a hero.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word is commonly substantivized for a person of courage or valor. Its application to a woman is reported but disputed in the lexical evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person whose powers have become weak.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A vulgar or nonstandard usage according to the lexical evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: False or vain things, especially unprofitable sayings.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural noun for false or futile utterances or things.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An idle, unoccupied, or lazy person; one diverted from profitable pursuits, and hence one given to joking, false speech, or unprofitable sport.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can emphasize idleness, lack of useful occupation, vain pursuits, joking, or speech without truth.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The unit supplies the Quranic nullity sense and the distinct blood-going-unavenged idiom.
